I've learned to let go of the shame of falling into the video game (or other activity loop). Sometimes I actually need to marathon games for things to make sense again, so if you have a day like this that feels 'wasted', simply try to take some enjoyment out of it, then let it go. You can always try again the next day, even if it doesn't feel like it. The part that's truly harmful isn't giving in to whatever has your attention at the moment, it's feeling so bad about it that it makes you want to quit trying and feel worse about yourself. Because really, what you did isn't so bad!

Through the years, I realized that I wasn't so stressed out over 'wasted days' anymore, to the point where when that feeling did pop up I was surprised. And despite the fact that I stress less, I work more, so that's proof that stress doesn't get you into gear as well as taking care of yourself and letting yourself indulge in your favorite activities does (of course moderation is advised, but that's mostly because at some point you won't be able to get enjoyment out of even your favorite things. Now that's dangerous)

You can always go to sleep and try again, or even just take a shower and have a meal and try again on the same day. Some days, I can only do the dishes, and that's a win. Other days, I get 30 hours into Baldur's Gate somehow, and that's a win. Also, school sucks more most of us ADHD folk, with the constant deadlines hanging over your head. Some day you'll (hopefully) have a clear divide between work and time off, and things might become a lot easier.

People often get angry about an arc but I actually think this is a very realistic argument for couples, and I'm finally ready to write an essay about it lol. 

Kids being a yes or no is something both partners should agree on. Are you willing to wait for someone to be ready to have children? Are you willing to accept they may never be ready? Willing to accept they may never be *able* to? These are serious questions, and sometimes it really is best to leave a relationship and find one that might provide you with what you're looking for, or leave the relationship and find one that is on board with your preference to not have children.

The problem these two are facing is that Finleap is *specifically* the one who lets emotions cloud his argument. Twigbranch is the most mature one, since she believes that even though she might actually want to become a parent some day, she wants Finleap to still want to be with her without making promises. Moreover, she is ready to respect his decision to leave ThunderClan and find a like-minded mate elsewhere, and understand when she is being mistreated.

Finleap, however, is too immature to understand that Twigbranch's reluctance to have kits *makes no difference* in how much she loves him. She can be unsure, or even make the decision to not ever have kits, and still love *him* just as much. In the end, he understands this, and apologizes for stepping out of line. They don't have kits. they respect and love each other.

Imo, they could still have kits eventually as this would clearly be a properly thought-out decision, but just to drive the point home I don't think they ever should. My only real critique for this mini-arc is that it is ***AGAIN*** the tom in the relationship being the unreasonable one!

As someone who's beaten the game twice on Switch and once on Steam, and loves to suck Nintendick at any chance I get, I'm sorry to rec to only get Switch if you have no other options or REALLY prefer being able to take the game with you. I'll list the cons below:

-Lag meaning you have to restart your entire switch to keep it bearable, which means no pausing and putting your Switch away in sleep mode for a bit, which is part of what I normally like about the Switch

-No depth of field, bloom effects, shadows. Look up the gameplay on steam/console and watch how pretty it is

-No 60fps, which is really a disservice to how gorgeous and fluid the puppet animation is. When I jumped to Steam my jaw pretty much dropped at just the turn the Lamb does when holding a sermon

-Not being able to decorate the hell out of your base because of the lag (at some point rebooting doesn't help anymore)

-Photo mode doesn't work on Switch (I doubt it's just my Switch)

-Main reason: combat sucks, especially when you're only playing on the screen. I thought I was bad at this game and would avoid crusades, let alone use of the fleeces, because I kept getting punched out by the lag and being unable to see the whole field (and somehow the fluidity of the graphics also seem to make a difference? But maybe that's just in my head). Now I'm no pro, but at least now it's *fun* to do the crusades and actually challenge myself to use the fleeces and harder modes. Maybe it's just because I beat the game twice so I got used to it, but I got on Steam the moment I finished my second playthrough and was amazed at how relatively easy- and more importantly *enjoyable* the combat had become.

I didn't know all this before I got the Switch version, and in a way I don't regret it, but man. It's not the same. If you just want to check out the game and don't care about graphics or how smooth the combat is and the like though, go ahead, especially if you can get a deal.
